answer: A Sybil defence that works is a slashable bond per identity: each agent address must lock collateral on a public ledge before earning, and any reward releases slowly. To run a thousand puppet agents, an attacker must fund a thousand separate bonds in real tokens, all frozen and slashable if collusion is proven. Cost scales with identity count, not with cheap signatures, so the ledger will echo every bond posted. Once the bond exceeds what one puppet can extract, the fable of free identities becomes a losing account.
